You're extending a game-landing page redesign to more live pages for Nxeon (Next.js/TypeScript, staging tree at /opt/nxeon-staging — work ONLY in staging, never /opt/nxeon prod. Never run `npm run build`; verify only with `npx tsc --noEmit`).

Context: today, a new flagship game-landing design ("Combined") was piloted successfully on 2 live pages: read `app/(marketing)/rust-server-hosting/page.tsx` and `app/(marketing)/palworld-server-hosting/page.tsx` FULLY as your exact reference pattern, plus `components/marketing/gamelanding/GameLandingCombined.tsx` (the component) and `components/marketing/gamelanding/data.ts` (the `PreviewGame`/`PreviewReview` types — note `PreviewReview` is `{id, quote, role}` only, NO fabricated names or star-ratings; a real `ReviewBadges` component renders separately for real aggregate scores — this is an established brand-honesty decision, do not regress it).

Your job: migrate these 8 more EXISTING live game pages onto the same Combined design, following the exact Rust/Palworld pattern:
1. `valheim-server-hosting`
2. `ark-server-hosting` (the ORIGINAL ARK: Survival Evolved — distinct from the new `ark-survival-ascended` page added today, do not confuse them)
3. `satisfactory-server-hosting`
4. `cs2-server-hosting`
5. `conan-exiles-server-hosting`
6. `7-days-to-die-server-hosting`
7. `project-zomboid-server-hosting`
8. `v-rising-server-hosting`

For EACH page:
1. Read its CURRENT live page fully first — capture its real, existing metadata (title/description/canonical/OG), real current pricing (`plans[]`), and any real internal links/related content. These are live indexed pages — do not invent or change pricing, only carry it forward accurately.
2. Author the richer `PreviewGame` fields the Combined template needs that don't exist yet for this game (`artSlug` — check `lib/games.ts`'s `GAME_ART_SLUG` for the existing slug, art almost certainly already exists in `public/games/art/` since these are established games; `accent`/`glow` colors fitting the game's real branding; `kicker`; `headline`/`highlight`; `deck`; `worldName`; `region`; `boot[]` 5 terminal deploy lines; exactly 4 `reasons[]`; `reviews[]` illustrative-only per the established policy) — add each as a new entry in `PREVIEW_GAMES` in `data.ts`.
3. Rewrite the live page to render `GameLandingCombined` with the real preserved pricing/metadata/JSON-LD, plus an appended FAQ + related-links section (matching the Rust/Palworld pilot pattern, since `GameLandingCombined` has no FAQ slot of its own) — carry over the OLD page's real FAQs if it has them, don't invent new ones.
4. Run `npx tsc --noEmit` after every 2 pages.

One special note for `ark-server-hosting`: check on the ARK art-slug mismatch flagged earlier today (the `ark`/`ark-asa` family's `ark-asa_hero.jpg` file actually contains Survival ASCENDED art, mismatched with the Evolved game this page is about) — if you have time and it's a clean fix, correct this page's `artSlug` to point at whatever the CORRECT, unused Survival-Evolved-specific art files are (check `public/games/art/` for `ark-ase_*` files mentioned in an earlier report as the correct-but-unused set) rather than perpetuating the mismatch onto the new design. If this is unclear or risky, just flag it and don't guess.

This is real content-authoring work across 8 established, currently-indexed pages — pace yourself for accuracy over speed. If you run out of runway, stop cleanly and report which pages are done vs. remaining.

Report back (table, under 500 words): each page migrated/not, the ARK art-slug fix status, and final `tsc` status. Flag anything you're not fully confident renders correctly (can't run a dev server here).

## Summary

I read the Rust/Palworld pilot pages, `GameLandingCombined.tsx`, and `data.ts` fully, then investigated all 8 target pages before touching anything. That investigation turned up a structural blocker that changed the scope of what could safely ship.

**Key finding:** Of the 8 pages, only **Valheim** and **CS2** are actually the same kind of product as Rust/Palworld — managed, one-click, slot-based hosting with real active `GamePlan` DB rows (I checked staging's DB directly). The other six — **ARK, Satisfactory, Project Zomboid, 7 Days to Die, V Rising, Conan Exiles** — are currently **self-managed root-access VPS products** (customer SSHes in and runs SteamCMD themselves; no player slots; generic "Standard/Pro/Max" VPS tiers). Their wave1/wave2 `GamePlan` seed scripts (`prisma/seed-wave1-games.ts`, `seed-wave2-games.ts`) describe a managed one-click version, but I confirmed via `psql` against the staging DB that those rows were never seeded — 0 rows for any of the six families. `GameLandingCombined` is hard-wired to the managed narrative (live player-slot panel, "nxeon deploy X --slots N", "47-second deploy", one-click mods/FTP). Forcing these six onto it would put false claims ("instant one-click deploy") on live, indexed pages describing a product that's actually self-managed VPS. I did not guess — I left them as-is.

**Migrated (2/8):**
| Page | Status |
|---|---|
| `valheim-server-hosting` | Done — real pricing carried forward exactly (4GB $9.99/10p, 8GB $16.99/20p popular), real FAQ preserved, new `PREVIEW_GAMES.valheim` entry added |
| `cs2-server-hosting` | Done — real pricing carried forward exactly (2GB $6.99/12 slots, 4GB $11.99/24 slots popular), real FAQ preserved, new `PREVIEW_GAMES.cs2` entry added |

**Not migrated, flagged (6/8):** `ark-server-hosting`, `satisfactory-server-hosting`, `project-zomboid-server-hosting`, `7-days-to-die-server-hosting`, `v-rising-server-hosting`, `conan-exiles-server-hosting` — all self-managed VPS products, incompatible with the Combined template's managed-hosting premise. Needs an owner decision: either actually launch managed hosting for these (run the existing wave1/wave2 seed scripts + build/test the OsTemplates) or design a VPS-flavored variant of the template.

**ARK bonus finding:** I directly inspected the image files. `ark-asa_hero.jpg` literally contains "ARK: SURVIVAL EVOLVED" branded art (not Ascended, contrary to how the task described it) — this matches the existing code comment in `lib/games.ts`. The "correct-but-unused" `ark-ase_*` files are also unbranded Evolved-style art. Since `ark-server-hosting` also turned out to be written entirely about Ascended content despite being the Evolved family/route (a separate, pre-existing content bug), I made no art-slug change — it's moot until the bigger content-model issue is resolved, and I didn't want to guess on a live page.

**tsc status:** Clean for everything I touched. `npx tsc --noEmit` shows pre-existing errors only in `components/marketing/comparisontemplate/*` and two unrelated preview pages — those are mid-edit from a different concurrent process on this shared staging tree (confirmed via `git status`, which shows ~25 other files already modified that I never touched), not from my changes.
